subdivision_of_building:
Double-Storey Side Extension
Full Roof Replacement - affecting the entire first floor.
Garage Conversion - will affect the entire garage and adjoining outbuilding.
description:
This proposal sets out a comprehensive remodelling and extension project for a commercial children’s nursery located in Hornchurch. Operating Monday to Friday, the nursery is in urgent need of redevelopment to address current space limitations and to create an environment that better supports the care, learning, and well-being of its children. The proposed works aim to deliver a modern, functional, and nurturing space that places safety, accessibility, and sustainability at its core.

The scope of the proposed development includes: Double-Storey Side Extension, Full Roof Replacement, Loft Conversion and a Garage Conversion (Change of use). It is important to note that the garage was originally granted planning permission under application reference P0463.93, a new planning application is required to facilitate the proposed conversion and ensure compliance with current regulations and local planning policies. The proposed garage conversion has been approved by Building Control under application reference BA/6024/25/3 to facilitate a change of use to form part of the commercial nursery.
decision_conditions: The proposed two storey side extension, roof remodelling and flat roof rear dormer would, by reason of its proportions, scale and design at this prominent location, appear as an incongruous development in relation to the existing host building, and visually intrusive feature in the street scene, and the surrounding area, especially from its junction with Winifred Avenue. As such, the proposal is contrary to Policies 7 & 26 of the Havering Local Plan 2021.

The additional scale to the business use, based on the available details would adversely affect the nearby residential amenity in terms of noise and general disturbance and therefore would be contrary to Policies 7, 26 and 34 of the Havering Local Plan 2021, which seek amongst other things high quality development that ensures that the amenity and quality of  life of existing residents is not adversely affected. These aims are reflected in the National Planning Policy Framework at Para 130(f).

Based on the proposed scale of the business use through additional intensity, would increase vehicle movement to and from the site over the existing use which would lead to increase demand for on-street parking and encourage users to wait in close proximity to the site potentially detrimental to highway and pedestrian safety. The proposals would likely increase parking pressure and congestion at peak times to the detriment of surrounding neighbouring amenity and the safe and free flow of traffic with potential impact upon highways safety for both pedestrian and vehicular traffic. There would be conflict with Havering Local Plan 2021 Policies 16, 17, 23 and 24 in addition to Paragraph 111 of the NPPF.

Statement Required by Article 35 (2) of the Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015: Consideration was given to seeking amendments, but given conflict with adopted planning policy, it was necessary to issue a decision as close to the statutory timeframe as possible as opposed to seeking amendments which would have significantly delayed the application.
